decision: Framed the upgrade as a durable state machine, not a higher tool-round limit
why: The brief already fixes the invariants, so the long run proceeds without a pause. Done means a 20-step run whose model context stays bounded, a crash resume that does not repeat a finished non-idempotent tool, and the existing suite still green.

decision: AI has no public one-tool executor, so the runtime cannot call tool procs directly
why: Validation, authorization, confirmation, timeout, and result limits live only inside CustomToolExecution, which generate uses after a model tool call.

decision: Base is working-state reducer with one perform_tool method
why: Candidate B keeps a live menu across tool steps so Jev chooses ids and the reasoner is not called every turn. Graft request-id idempotency and seal-wipe-on-terminal. Drop lease epoch, grant_confirmation, and the 8-step default. Cross-judge seats on Claude and GPT did not start.

decision: Continued the durable runtime after the earlier framing rows
why: Those rows stop at the design choice. This run implements, proves, and documents it.

decision: Kept the working-state reducer and one Runtime loop
why: A second engine would duplicate the ledger. Engine stays the shell and calls Runtime when the plan has candidates.

why: Push to bowerbird-app/RecordingStudio_AI returned 403. Gemfile stays on tag v0.4.0. Tool steps raise ConfigurationError until AI 0.5.0 is published.

why: Stopping on the first plan's reasoner call made a one-reasoner budget fail before any tool. Step, tool, and runtime caps still stop the loop.
